programs.next_step: Step 1: write the short application (12-page form, pitch deck of up to ten slides, three-minute video pitch) on the EU Funding and Tenders portal under topic HORIZON-EIC-2026-ACCELERATOR-01; short proposals may be submitted at any time and are batched every first Tuesday of the month at 17:00 Brussels time, with feedback in about 4-6 weeks. On a GO, Step 2: prepare the full application (20-page form, pitch deck, implementation plan, financial information, letters of intent, FTO analysis, three-minute video) and submit it to a batching date; the last 2026 cut-off on the page is 4 November 2026 at 17:00 Brussels time. Step 3: pitch to the EIC Jury if invited. The founder, as the company's account holder on the portal, clicks submit.
programs.notes: Four-step process: short application (any time, batched first Tuesday monthly), full application (2026 batching dates written on the page as 7/01/2026, 04/03/2026, 06/05/2026, 08/07/2026, 02/09/2026, 04/11/2026, all 17:00 Brussels time; remote result in 8-9 weeks), interview with the EIC Jury (an interview session is organised after each second batch; results 2-3 weeks after the interview week), then grant agreement signature and due diligence for the investment component (decided within 2-6 months). Only one application at a time; a new one only after results of the previous. Grant only is provided once per company during Horizon Europe 2021-2027. Mid-caps (up to 499 employees) can apply for investment only; UK applicants grant only; third-country applicants must relocate before Step 2. Two strands: Accelerator Open (any field of technology, EUR 414 million budget in 2026) and Accelerator Challenges (pre-defined topics, EUR 220 million in 2026). Top-ranked full proposals corresponding to 2.5 times the available grant budget are invited to interview; proposals above the 13/15 threshold that are not funded receive a Seal of Excellence. Fast Track (existing Horizon projects) and Plug-In (certified national programmes) schemes go straight to the full application stage. The page does not state an open or closed status; it lists the 2026 cut-offs and links to the portal topic. Re-read the status page before quoting any 2027 date.

Swedish, Finnish and Danish partners also file a national application with their agency. The founder, as lead applicant, clicks submit on the platform.
programs.notes: No Eurostars call is open on 2026-10-15: the Eureka open-calls listing shows no Eurostars call, and Call 12 opens 17 December 2026 with deadline 4 March 2027 14:00 CET; calls are usually organised twice a year. Seven international eligibility criteria: SME lead from a Eurostars country; at least two independent entities; at least two Eurostars countries with at least one organisation from an EU or Horizon Europe associated country; SMEs from Eurostars countries carry 50% or more of the budget excluding subcontracting; no single participant or country above 70% of the budget; duration 36 months or less; exclusive focus on civil applications. Funding is decentralised: Eureka pays nothing, each partner's national funding body pays under national rules and may cap amounts. National details for Call 12 were marked as being confirmed and subject to change before the call opens. Sweden: Vinnova funds SMEs up to 50% of costs, max 5 MSEK per project; Swedish participants submit a national application to Vinnova after a positive evaluation; Vinnova checks the latest registered annual report and credit reports. Finland: Business Finland requires a parallel national application with attachments when the Eurostars application is submitted. Denmark: IFD max 300 000 EUR per participant (500 000 EUR for several Danish participants, min 50 000 EUR); upload the application to e-grant within 14 days after the deadline. Norway: the funder is the Research Council of Norway, not Innovasjon Norge. Iceland: Rannís, max 45 MISK per project. Greece, Israel, Italy and Brussels have no budget for this call.

The founder clicks submit.
programs.notes: Continuously open with no cut-off dates; the page says access can be granted within two working days. Process from the Terms of Reference V3 (31/03/2026): eligibility check by self-assessment plus ethics self-assessment, then technical assessment by the requested AI Factory, then first-come-first-served until the call's reserved resources are exhausted. Innovation is the decisive factor of the final decision. One Playground award per project lead at a time; no extensions and no additional resources; final report due three months after the allocation ends; results must be published except confidential parts and EuroHPC JU plus the AI Factory acknowledged; only proposals in English, with a civilian purpose and compliant with the AI Act; no double-awarding with a running EuroHPC allocation. The organisation proves its status with a valid VAT number and, if applicable, a PIC. The hour table on the page is an image: 5 000 GPU hours on every listed partition (read 2026-10-15); partition availability may be limited by demand. Apply Now on the page links to the portal root; the portal is a JavaScript app so the call number could not be verified from outside it. Questions: aif.access@eurohpc-ju.europa.eu.

The founder clicks submit.
programs.notes: Continuously open with two cut-off dates per month that trigger evaluation; the page says approval within ten working days from the cut-off; specific cut-off dates are not listed on the page. Process: eligibility check, technical assessment by the AI Factory, expert evaluation by the AI Factory's Industrial Innovation Group on two criteria, innovation and impact, each scored 0 to 5 with a threshold of 3 per criterion and 6 overall, then a ranked list approved by the EuroHPC JU Executive Director. EIC Accelerator challenge awardees pass without further evaluation and have priority within the cut-off. Proposals below the per-system minimum request are administratively rejected; awards may be reduced in scope. Normally one Large Scale award per project lead at a time; proposals submitted after a cut-off roll into the next one; appeals to aif.access@eurohpc-ju.europa.eu within 15 days. No extensions or top-ups; final report three months after the end; English, civilian purpose, AI Act compliance, no double-awarding. Continuation proposals are possible with a progress or final report.

The project lead clicks submit.
programs.notes: Opened 15 May 2025; continuously open with a cut-off every two months. Cut-off dates on the page: 27 Feb, 30 Apr, 30 Jun, 1 Sep, 30 Oct and 11 Dec 2026 and 31 Dec 2033, all 10:00 CET (the Full Call Details PDF says 31 August instead of 1 September). Access starts at most one month after the cut-off. Process: administrative check, technical assessment by the hosting entity, peer review by two independent experts on excellence, innovation and impact, and quality and efficiency of implementation, each 0 to 5 with a threshold of 3 per criterion and 10 overall, then first-come-first-served until the cut-off's resources are depleted. EU-funded projects already evaluated by expert panels skip the expert evaluation and have priority. Proposals not following the template are administratively rejected. At most 10 percent of the allocation may go to inference. One AI for Science award per project lead at a time. Extensions of up to three months possible on request one month before the end. SMEs and startups doing private AI innovation are expected to use the Industrial Innovation modes; the company-in-EU-project exception cannot be expressed as a matcher rule, so ask. The hour table on the page is an image (read 2026-10-15): minimum 20 000 and maximum 90 000 node hours on each listed partition. Terms of Reference dated 20/05/2025. Questions: access@eurohpc-ju.europa.eu.

Finnish companies can use both the EuroHPC JU calls and national routes: a Business Finland computing capacity grant, nationally funded RDI projects with academia, or paid commercial access.

The founder clicks submit on the form and later on the chosen application.
programs.notes: Consortium countries Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Norway and Poland can use both EuroHPC JU calls and national access opportunities; AI Factory antennas are Belgium, Iceland, Latvia and Switzerland; other EU member states and Horizon Europe associated countries get computing only through EuroHPC JU calls. The national route is state aid: the company must know it has not used up its national state aid (maximum 300 000 euro in three years) and must report the value of the resources used. Free access is for RDI, not for 24/7 or commercial deployment. The project idea is evaluated on technical feasibility and risk; usually starts with a small pilot. A short final report is required after an EU-funded computing project; an NDA can cover sensitive parts. Commercial paid access is currently possible for Finnish companies. Datasets are free only for a research project granted LUMI resources. Fully confidential projects are pointed to national mechanisms such as Business Finland. The page gives no hour caps or durations.

Ordinary national e-infrastructure allocations run through metacenter.no with a call in January (allocations from 1 April) and one in June (from 1 October), deadlines usually in February and August, open to industrial parties, but the user contribution model prices commercial and industry users (category C) at market price, 35 NOK per GPU-hour from 1 October 2025, so free GPU hours for a Norwegian company come through the EuroHPC AI Factory calls rather than the national allocation. Olivia is a Cray EX system with 448 GPUs for researchers across Norway. The English language link (/node/406) serves the same Norwegian content.

The PI clicks submit.
programs.notes: Resources are free for researchers at Swedish universities and research institutes and authorised by the Swedish Research Council. Small: technical evaluation within a week, reviewed weekly all year. Medium: technical evaluation, monthly, submission before the 15th. Large: scientific and technical evaluation twice a year by NAC; the Large Fall 2026 deadline is 16 October 2026 at 15:00 CEST, decisions in November, projects start 1 January 2027 for 6 or 12 months, and there are now upper limits on the capacity you can request. A PI cannot hold compute in a Medium and a Large project at the same time. Alvis and Tetralith are decommissioned, Bianca this autumn and Dardel on 1 January 2027. LUMI Sweden rounds now accept CPU-only requests. No GPU hour figures are published on these pages. Industry access is not mentioned.

Access is granted by NSC via SUPR; access to one node type does not automatically grant the other. The Wallenberg funding requirement is the gate the matcher cannot express; ask about it. The NSC pages say documentation is moving to hpc.pages.naiss.se and older NSC pages may be outdated. Industry is not mentioned.
